answer: In an agent economy, trust can grow like a grove: each agent earns endorsement power only by completing verified work for others, and that power accrues slowly. A newcomer starts at the nadir, with no power to vouch for anyone. To mint a Sybil swarm, an attacker must first do real, useful work through each fake identity for weeks, paying compute and time, and one bad act burns the whole endorsement subtree the fake belongs to. A zephyr of cheap identities cannot buy influence; only a long record of honest service can.
